title: Repair the coat check
prompt:
coat_check(slips) takes a list of slips, each a (color, size) pair, and returns the ticket number each slip gets. Tickets start at 0, and a new coat gets the next number. Two lines are wrong.

The slip. It only writes down the color, so a red M and a red L count as the same coat. It should hold the color and the size.

The hit. When the slip is already in the notebook, it hands out a new number. It should hand back the ticket stored there.
hints: Try the two samples by hand. In the first, what should the second `red M` slip get? In the second, are `red M` and `red L` the same coat?
The slip has to say everything that makes one coat different from another. `(color, size)` is a tuple, and a tuple can be a dict key.
On a hit, append `notebook[slip]`. That is the ticket the coat got the first time.
explain: The slip `(color, size)` describes exactly one coat, so a red M and a red L get different hooks. When the slip is already in the notebook, `notebook[slip]` is the hook that coat already hangs on, and no new hook is used. Swap coats for nodes and this is the table lesson 1.1 asks you to repair.
